## Historical audit — S0148, chunk 1 of 2

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/C2/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines in this file. No images or other chunk were inspected.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Goal: line 1, student `model_request` | Reconstruct a single indoor RGB image as editable SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching camera, objects, materials and occlusion. The student’s identification of an industrial kitchen is a visual interpretation, not independently checked here. |
| Initial build: lines 3–5, student `model_response`, step-1 `execute` and `execution_result` | The program constructs multiple owners: architecture, posts, cabinetry, oven, island, hood and kettle. Island parts include drawers, sink and faucet; the oven and kettle also have grouped components. It specifies procedural timber and hood textures, metallic tap materials, a camera, world and lights. The runner reports `ok: true` and saves a render and blend file. Code-level ownership and stated support heights do not verify physical contact, collisions or reference fidelity. |
| Camera probe: lines 8–12 | The student received the first render, result and scheduling evidence, then estimated that the island and hood were too low and the post too broad. Step 2 introduced vertical lens shift `(0, -0.075)`, predicting an upward image shift while retaining geometry and appearance; execution returned `ok: true`. These are the student’s visual estimates and prediction, not independent measurements. |
| Hood revision: lines 15–19 | After receiving step 2, the student claimed improved vertical framing but remaining shallow island slopes, broad post, left-shifted oven and flat lighting. Step 3 changed hood center, width, depth and top, with dependent parts parameterized with it; camera and appearance were retained. It returned `ok: true`. Kettle occlusion was a student hypothesis, not established visibility. |
| Selection and scope: lines 20–21 | Two `select` events record step 3. All three visible builds produced saved images, but the images themselves are unavailable to this audit; selection is not a formal visual-quality verdict. Overall outcome beyond this chunk is **unknown**, not an established algorithm failure or technical interruption. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No separate teacher message, detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in this chunk, so teacher receipt or adoption cannot be claimed. The system’s shared procedure and the runner’s feedback are visible inputs, not evidence of a separate teacher. The student independently chose the camera and hood probes after prompted comparisons; the recorded CLI sessions report no tool calls (lines 2, 9, 16).

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, an operational render validates execution, not scene correctness; separating a camera probe from a single-owner revision makes their intended effects easier to interpret. Task-specific hypotheses—hood silhouette, post width, appliance placement, lighting and shadow mismatch—remain unverified. The code includes multiple objects, textures, grouped parts and explicit poses, but neither object visibility, material appearance, attachment integrity nor camera/light accuracy is independently established. The later chunk may contain further events, but none are inferred here.
